key_insight: Zero-real Agent Policy (ZAP) separates robot intelligence into understanding what to do and learning how to move. It combines pretrained vision-language knowledge with simulation-based training to turn task understanding into robot control.
problem_solved: Robot policies must connect language and visual scene understanding to effective physical actions, including when familiar task elements appear in new combinations.
method: Use a pretrained 27B-parameter vision-language model to bootstrap world understanding and reasoning.
Apply supervised fine-tuning and GRPO on simple simulated tasks to teach robot movement.
Connect the model to robot control through a simple tool harness.
impact: ZAP offers practitioners a recipe for combining pretrained understanding with simulation-trained control rather than learning both from scratch. The abstract does not report quantitative results, so the extent of compositional generalization remains unspecified here.
visual_elements: Split diagram: pretrained model supplies 'what'; simulation training supplies 'how'.
Training pipeline: vision-language model → supervised fine-tuning → GRPO → robot policy.
Control-loop illustration: scene and instruction → model → tool harness → robot action.
Compositional task grid showing familiar objects, instructions, and actions recombined into new tasks.
paper_title: Pretraining Knows What, Simulation Teaches How: Compositional Generalization in a Sim-Trained Robot Agent
paper_authors: Benjamin Pikus, Daniel Saunders, Mircea Mironenco, Salman Mohammadi, Mathew Mathew
